files..exo/githooks/commit-msg:
#!/bin/sh
# exo: runs `exo hook commit-msg`. Turn the hooks off with governance.githooks: false
# in .exo/config.json. Skipping them with --no-verify is possible; CI still runs
# `exo check`.
project="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
if [ -n "${EXO_HOOK_CMD:-}" ]; then
  exec $EXO_HOOK_CMD hook commit-msg --project "$project" "$@"
fi
if command -v exo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  exec exo hook commit-msg --project "$project" "$@"
fi
echo "exo: not found in PATH, so the commit-msg hook did not run; CI still runs exo check" >&2
exit 0

# Canvas: <change-name>

## Requirements

<!-- What the change must do, in the spec's words: the requirement IDs (CAP-<cap>-FR-n) and scenarios (S-n) it covers. -->

## Entities

<!-- The domain objects involved, with the fields and invariants the code must respect. -->

## Approach

<!-- The chosen solution in a few lines, and why it beats the alternatives considered. -->

## Structure

<!-- Where the code goes: files and modules to create or change, and how they depend on each other. -->

## Operations

<!-- The steps the code performs, in order, including the unhappy paths. Each one maps to code the review can find. -->

## Norms

<!-- The conventions the code follows: naming, error handling, logging, testing, the project's own rules. -->

## Safeguards

<!-- What must never happen: security and data limits, invariants, performance bounds, threats from the threat model. -->

# Gate: <gate>

<!--
One file per gate: <change-root>/gates/<gate>.md, written by the skill that runs the gate.
Keep the marker below with the gate name (snake_case, the same as the file name):
`exo gate publish` uses it to keep a single PR comment per gate.
-->

<!-- exo-gate:<gate> -->

## Verdict

<!-- APPROVED or ESCALATED, then one sentence of reason: "APPROVED: no blocking finding." -->

## Findings

<!--
| Severity | File:line | Finding | Rule/OWASP |
|---|---|---|---|
| High | src/auth/login.py:42 | User input reaches the SQL query unescaped | CWE-89, A05:2025 Injection |
-->

## Approval

<!--
Requires tech_lead approval: yes | no
Source: skill <skill name>
"yes" when the verdict is ESCALATED or a Critical or High finding stays open.
-->

files..exo/shared/templates/spec.md:
# Spec: <change-name>

<!--
A delta over the living specs (specs/capabilities/<capability>/spec.md), ADR-0013.
Keep only the sections you need, with at least one requirement in total.
Requirement IDs: CAP-<capability>-FR-n or CAP-<capability>-NFR-n. New IDs take the
next free number of the capability; removed IDs are never reused.
Scenario IDs: S-n, unique in this change, so design.md and test-spec.md can cite them.
`exo specs merge <change>` applies this delta by ID.
-->

## ADDED Requirements

<!--
### CAP-<capability>-FR-<n>: <title>
The system SHALL ...

#### Scenario S-1: <title>
- Given ...
- When ...
- Then ...
-->

## MODIFIED Requirements

<!-- Same shape as ADDED: the full new text of an existing requirement, with its scenarios. -->

## REMOVED Requirements

<!--
### CAP-<capability>-FR-<n>: <title>
Reason: <why it is removed>
-->

## Scope

<!-- What is tested and at which levels (unit, integration, e2e). -->

|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-1 | S-1, CAP-<capability>-FR-<n> | unit | ... | pytest tests/test_x.py::test_y |
-->

## Traceability

<!-- Every ADDED or MODIFIED requirement (CAP-<capability>-FR-n, CAP-<capability>-NFR-n) and every
scenario S-n of the delta, with the test cases that cover it. `exo speclint` checks that none is missing. -->

<!-- One of: ready | needs-rework | blocked -->

<!-- CAP-<capability>-FR-n -> the test that proves it, for every ADDED or MODIFIED requirement. -->

## Scenario Coverage

<!-- S-n -> the test that exercises it, for every scenario of the delta. -->

## Issues Found

<!-- Severity | path:line | impact | suggested fix. "None" if nothing. -->

## Tests

<!-- Exact command, passed / failed, pre-existing failures. -->
